title: Prove your standard: buyer packs, training and audits

say: Prove your standard: buyer packs, training and audits.
This is the video for module three of Product Standardisation and Compliance.
When a supermarket or hotel considers a new supplier, the buyer must convince her manager. Clear documents make her job easy.

say: Keep this pack as PDFs on your phone. A data sheet summarises your spec for buyers. For example, Funmi weighs a filled jar at 160 grams. 24 jars plus a 300 gram carton gives 4,140 grams, about 4.1 kilograms.
Send copies with a watermark, never originals.

panel.heading: Ready to send the same day

say: Answer supplier forms truthfully. A dated plan, like registration expected by March, is better than a false yes.
Send samples from a normal batch, and keep retained samples from every batch you sell.

say: Train and sign off the safety steps before production steps. A learner should know where the lid, first aid box and exit are before she touches the pot.

say: Every quarter, gather your spec, SOPs, label and records. Watch one batch being made without helping, and note where practice differs.

say: Ask of each gap: does a buyer I want require it, and could it harm a customer? A pharmacy chain she wants asks about recalls, so traceability is her priority. Free fixes, like an old SOP on the wall, happen this week.

panel.rule: Pick one priority: buyers need it and it protects customers.

say: The plan has three blocks: set up, run and record, then check and prove.
In week one she adds supplier name and supplier batch number columns to her records, in a new record book for about 2,000 naira.
In week two she retrains both helpers and adds a retained sample shelf, for about 5,000 naira.
Near the end she runs a mock recall, tracing a batch to its materials and customers within 2 hours. That is strong proof for any buyer.
Now build your buyer pack and start a retained sample box. Make your skills matrix and display your stop rule. Then run your audit and write your 90-day plan with one measurable target.
